findings.title: Branch attribution change lacks security sign-off
findings.problem: security-practices.md 'CRITICAL: Project & User Attribution Headers' (rule 2) and the git-workflow.md review checklist make any change to the derivation source of branch attribution a CRITICAL change needing security-review sign-off. This change derives Cowork events' git_branch and summary branch_dominant from the host folder via detectGitBranch (CoworkEventProducer.ts:317, cowork-events.ts:348-352), overwrites any transcript branch and deletes branch_counts; no sign-off is recorded.
findings.impact: Branch attribution drives analytics attribution across repositories and branches; the project guide forbids merging a change to its derivation without security review, so the documented workflow is not met.
findings.recommendation: Mark the PR CRITICAL in its description, complete the security-practices.md reviewer checklist for attribution changes, and obtain and record security-review sign-off before merge. No source edit is needed; the derivation already uses the canonical detectGitBranch() helper the guide's Good example names.
findings.check_notes: evidence finding: fix_evidence maps only a decision record (sign-off requested, not given); no artifact or command proves the PR callout or a recorded sign-off

decision.outcome: addressed in the PR description: the change is called out as a CRITICAL branch-attribution change with security-review sign-off requested on the PR before merge
decision.rationale: The PR description's Summary now carries the CRITICAL callout the checklist of security-practices.md ('CRITICAL: Project & User Attribution Headers') asks for: it names the derivation source change of git_branch and branch_dominant on Cowork events, from the transcript's gitBranch to detectGitBranch() of the session's folder, a failed lookup giving no branch, and requests security-review sign-off before merge. The sign-off itself is a reviewer's act on the PR and cannot exist before the PR is opened. No source change: the derivation uses the canonical detectGitBranch() the guide names as the good example and treats a failure as no attribution.

disposition.rationale: Security-review sign-off is requested on the PR, called out as a CRITICAL branch-attribution change in its description, and is given there before merge; no code change is needed.

findings.title: Sandbox branch assertion bypasses Git env scrub
findings.problem: The assertion added to the existing sandbox test (git_branch must be '') sits outside the nested describe that deletes GIT_* from process.env and stubs GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/NOSYSTEM. detectGitBranch runs git via execAsync with the inherited environment, so an exported GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE points it at the outer repository and it reports that branch.
findings.impact: The test can fail spuriously when run inside a git hook (lint-staged in .husky/pre-commit runs tests for changed files) or with the temp dir inside a repository, the hazard the new describe's own comment names; reachability depends on whether the hook exports GIT_DIR and was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Run the git_branch '' assertion under the same GIT_* scrub the nested 'the branch of the session's folder' describe uses (delete GIT_* from process.env and stub GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM for that test), or move the assertion into that describe, so an exported GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE cannot point detectGitBranch at the outer repository.
findings.check_notes: HEAD source: file-level beforeAll (lines 164-176) deletes GIT_* and sets empty GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL + NOSYSTEM before every test, sandbox assertion included; restored in afterAll

decision.outcome: fixed in code (commit 968dc2c4, test(analytics): keep the Cowork producer tests free of outer git state)
decision.rationale: src/telemetry/runtime/cowork/__tests__/CoworkEventProducer.test.ts now removes every GIT_* variable of the outer process and points GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL at an empty file with GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 once for the whole file (file-level beforeAll / afterAll, restored after), so every test - the producer's git calls and the tests' own repositories - is independent of an exported GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE and of the developer's git config; the nested describe's own copy was removed. Proof: with GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE exported to the repository itself and the session's fallback working directory created, the sandbox test fails on 2ccd7a1f (cwd codemie-ai/codemie-code instead of Cowork) and passes on 968dc2c4; the whole file passes 50 / 50 under the exported variables.
